title: The kernels w_j/(c·|w|ⁿ) are locally integrable (Step 2)
statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, j ∈ Fin n and c ∈ ℝ. Define K(w) := w_j/(c·|w|^{m+1}) on ℝⁿ = Eucl n, where w_j is the j-th coordinate and division by 0 gives 0 (so K(0) = 0, and K ≡ 0 if c = 0). Then K is locally integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure: every point has a neighbourhood on which K is integrable.
lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (j : Fin (m + 1)) (c : ℝ), LocallyIntegrable (fun t : Eucl (m + 1) => t j / (c * ‖t‖ ^ (m + 1)))
